issues.description: Unguarded ET.parse lets malformed or hostile XML abort the whole ingest instead of producing a structured malformed_row warning.
NaN scores bypass clamp checks and can crash SQLite insertion or persist invalid numeric state.
Format B assumes metrics is a dict; truthy non-dict metrics values crash with AttributeError.
Format B coerces missing id/model/benchmark fields to strings or empty values instead of rejecting malformed rows.
Format C accepts missing run id, model, and task as empty strings, causing bad rows and possible UNIQUE-key collisions.
Ingest only upserts parsed records, so rows from files removed or skipped in a later run remain stale in results.
Model aliases are insert-only and never reconciled, so reports can show aliases no longer present in current results.
Empty-directory ingest returns an error only after creating and schema-initializing the requested database file.
Tests are fixture-heavy and miss malformed XML, non-finite scores, invalid nested JSON types, and changed-input reingest behavior.
